title: Bioenergetic cost of making an adenosine triphosphate molecule in animal mitochondria
authors: Watt IN, Montgomery MG, Runswick MJ, Leslie AG, Walker JE
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
population: F1-c-ring complex prepared from ATP synthase purified from bovine heart mitochondria
funder: This work was funded by the Medical Research Council.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
result: In the 3.5 Å crystal structure of the bovine F1-c-ring complex (PDB 2xnd), the c-ring has eight c subunits, so eight protons are translocated per 360° rotation, which produces three ATP: 2.7 protons per ATP. c-Subunit sequences are identical in almost all vertebrates. For each two electrons transferred to oxygen from NADH or succinate, ten or six protons are thought to be pumped out of the matrix; ADP/ATP exchange and phosphate-proton symport add one proton, a cost of 3.7 protons per ATP supplied to the cytoplasm, predicting P/O ratios of 2.7 and 1.6, close to experimental values of 2.5 and 1.5. The proton-motive force generated by respiration drives ATP synthesis.
